title: PRD: KV rehydration + canary simulated-traffic and observability acceptance criteria
creator: Maya Chen
description: Summary: After the recent multi-region latency incident where cold prefix misses and KV cache stalls produced a measurable SLO regression for 99th-percentile tail latency, the postmortem recommended three operational controls be encoded into the PRD. This ticket captures PRD-level requirement updates: (1) automatic KV rehydration (rehydrate/rehash prefixes proactively on scale events), (2) a standardized canary simulated-traffic harness that runs before route/fallback rollouts, and (3) explicit observability and acceptance criteria so on-call and release engineers can validate behavior without manual deep-dive. The intent is to make these controls first-class product requirements referenced by runtime, dedicated, and private deployments.
objectives: Define functional PRD requirements for automatic KV rehydration triggered by warm-pool fills, autoscale events, and tenant-burst detection
Specify a canary simulated-traffic suite that validates cache-warmth, tail-latency, and fallback routing before full cutover
Add measurable observability signals and alerting thresholds tied to acceptance gates
Create rollout and rollback criteria that map incident postmortem actions to release gates
background: Context: A high-severity incident revealed two failure modes: slow KV cache population under parallel coldstarts and routing-induced amplification when fallback rules shifted traffic across regions. The postmortem action items emphasized automated mitigation (rehydration), pre-cutover verification (simulated traffic canaries), and clearer acceptance criteria for SRE/Release engineers. Existing PRDs lack explicit requirements for automated cache priming and a reproducible canary harness. This work removes ambiguity by turning postmortem actions into discrete PRD items with ownerable acceptance tests.
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: The PRD defines a deterministic KV rehydration API contract (inputs, expected TTL behavior, idempotency guarantees) and a recommended default rehydration window for hosted customers
AC-2: The PRD includes a minimal policy matrix showing when rehydration is automatic vs opt-in (conditions: warm pool fill, autoscale > X, tenant burst > Y requests/min)
AC-3: The PRD specifies a canary simulated-traffic harness that can run in isolated canary clusters and produces a pass/fail report within 10 minutes
AC-4: The canary harness includes tests for cold-prefetch hit-rate >= 85% after rehydration, 99th-percentile tail latency within baseline + 30ms, and no increase in error-rate beyond 0.1%
AC-5: The PRD lists exact observability signals to be emitted (cache_fill_rate, cache_miss_ratio_by_prefix, kv_rehydrate_ops, simulated_canary_pass_rate) and their default alert thresholds

AC-6: Release gates: a rollout to production requires a green canary pass, cache_miss_ratio reduction of >= 40% vs unrehydrated baseline, and update to release notes documenting fallback budget implications
AC-7: Operator runbook in PRD references the automated rollback path if simulated canary triggers more than 3 failing prefixes or if tail latency increases > 25% vs baseline
decisions: Decision-1: Use a platform-level rehydration service (implemented in runtime) rather than per-model ad-hoc scripts to ensure consistent semantics across dedicated and private deployments
Decision-2: Canary simulated traffic will be defined as a parameterized suite (replay + synthetic mixes) that teams can run with tenant-specific prompt sets
Decision-3: Observability signals must be exported to the Console with a standard tagset so on-call can filter by tenant, region, and model family
tasks: Write PRD section: 'KV rehydration API and policy matrix' (owner: PM)
Draft canary simulated-traffic spec with traffic mixes and pass/fail thresholds (owner: PM + SRE)
Align runtime ENG on API contract and instrumentation points (owner: ENG lead)
Define default alert thresholds and dashboard widgets for Console (owner: Observability)
Create operator runbook snippets that map canary outcomes to rollout behavior (owner: SRE)
Coordinate security review for telemetry and synthetic traffic payloads (owner: PM)
Add PRD acceptance checklist to release playbook and link to automated CI job that runs canary suite
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Over-aggressive rehydration increases token/nvram usage and cost. Mitigation: Add policy caps and cost accounting; expose opt-in for private deployments.
Risk: Canary false positives due to synthetic traffic mismatch. Mitigation: Allow prompt-set parameterization and seed real traffic replays where safe.
Risk: Observability noise from high-cardinality tags. Mitigation: Require a curated tagset and sample rates in PRD
notes: This PRD fragment will be discussed at the 2026-03-16 triage and should be ready for formal review by runtime and observability by 2026-03-21. Post-review, the PRD will be linked from release playbooks and the SRE on-call checklist.
